answer: Anchor each agent identity to one surveyed parcel in a public land registry; a verifier accepts only one active identity per parcel and rejects duplicate parcel claims. The rule requires a mappable boundary feature, such as an inlet shoreline, a raven roost, or a basalt outcrop, so n sybils need n parcels. Each parcel pays property tax C per period; with per-period reward at most R, total profit n(R-C) is positive only while R>C. Registry collusion or subdivision remains the weak point.
